photos.description: The National museum (Czech: Národní muzeum) is a Czech museum institution intended to systematically establish, prepare and publicly exhibit natural scientific and historical collections. It was founded 1818 in Prague by Kašpar Maria Šternberg. Historian František Palacký was also strongly involved. The main museum building is located on the upper end of Wenceslas Square and was built by prominent Czech neo-renaissance architect Josef Schulz from 1885 - 1891;before this the museum had been temporarily based at several noblemen’s palaces. With the construction of a permanent building for the museum, a great deal of work which had previously been devoted to ensuring that the collections would remain intact was now put toward collecting new materials. The building was damaged during World War II in 1945 by a bomb, but the collections were not damaged because they had been moved to other storage sites. The museum reopened after intensive repairs in 1947, and in 1960 exterior night floodlighting was installed, which followed a general repair of the facade that had taken place in previous years. [Wikipedia.org]

photos.description: This image shows the Žižkov Television Tower, a distinctive landmark in Prague, Czech Republic. The tower is known for its unusual architecture, featuring three massive concrete pillars supporting various pod-like structures and observation decks. Designed by architects Václav Aulický and Jiří Kozák, it stands at a height of 216 meters, making it one of the tallest structures in the city. Completed in 1992, the tower serves as a telecommunications and observation facility, offering panoramic views of Prague. The structure is famous not only for its design but also for the unique sculptures of crawling babies by artist David Černý, which were added in 2000. The tower has been a subject of both admiration and controversy due to its unconventional appearance, but it has become a popular tourist attraction and a symbol of modern architecture in Prague.
